 :Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 04092019 at about 10.20 a.m., the Petitioner was proceeding in a car bearing No.KA51MB7497 near Jangli Peer Darga, Vijaypura Town, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore District.
At that time, a Bolero vehicle bearing No.KA07M5903 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's car.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Ashwini hospital and thereafter she was shifted to Aster CMI hospital wherein she was treated as an inpatient.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was doing business under the name and style of Lakshmi Saree House and was earning a sum of Rs.70,000/ p.m.
Due to the accident, she has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending car and therefore, both Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
3. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.1, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of car bearing NO.KA07M5903.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it admitted the issuance of policy in respect of car bearing NO.KA 07M5903 in favour of respondent No.2.
It is further contended that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by its driver.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of driver of car of petitioner and the petition is liable to be dismissed for nonjoinder of necessary parities.

Further contended that the driver of offending car was not holding valid and effective licence to drive the car and the insured has willfully handed over the vehicle to the driver who was not authorized to drive the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

sentences.text: In the Objection Statement, the Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending car.
There is also denial of the fact that the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
It is further contended that the accident was caused solely due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing No.KA51MB7497.
The driver of offending vehicle did possessed valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle as on the date of incident.
The offending vehicle had been issued valid and effective policy as on the date of incident by the respondent No.1.
Such being the case, respondent No.1 being the insurer of this respondent shall be made liable to compensate the petitioner and no liability may be saddled against this respondent.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 04092019 at about 10.00 a.m., near Jangli Peer Darga, on Devanahalli Vijayapura road, Vijayapura town, Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bolero bearing No.KA07M5903?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so.
How much and from whom?

3. What Order or Award?
5.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 21 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.21.
She also got examined doctor as P.W.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P22 and 23 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 04092019 at about 10.00 a.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA07 M5903 by its driver.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA07M5903 by its driver.
9. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, she got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 21 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P21.
P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in her chief affidavit.

Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 are the certified copies of FIR along with complaint, spot panchanama,
IMV report, charge sheet and Wound certificate.
Ex.P.6 is the certified copy of driving licence.
Ex.P.7 to 10 are the Discharge summaries.
Ex . P.11
is the medical bills, Ex.P.12 is the cash paid receipts, Ex.P.13 is the notarised copy of Aadhar card and Ex. P.14 to 21 are Xrays.

10. Upon going through Ex.P1 i.e., FIR along with Complaint, same is evident that on the complaint lodged before Vijayapura Police station, the SHO of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of offending vehicle bearing No.KA07M5903 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.

Ex.P.2 i.e., the copy of Spot Mahazar with sketch justifies that same is drawn in the presence of panchas, The document Ex.P.3 i.e., the certified copy of IMV report justify the fact of involvement of the two vehicles in the accident and the said document also discloses that the cause of accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in question.

The charge sheet document marked at Ex.P.4 discloses the fact that after thorough investigation IO has charge sheeted the driver of car bearing No.KA07M 5903 for the offences punishable under Secs.279, 338, 304A of IPC.

The document Ex.P.5 i.e.,
wound certificate discloses that as a result of RTA the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
11. Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 and got marked clinical notes and Xray at Ex.P.22 and 23.
He also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
12. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross examination P.W.1 has withstood the evidence deposed by her during her examination in chief.
Though several suggestions have been made to the witness, nothing worth to discard the evidence of PW.1 has been elicited.

Apart from this, the PW.1 has denied the other suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.1.
13.
Further, the Respondents have not adduced any evidence to rebut the evidence of petitioner.
In addition to this, the IO after thorough investigation filed a charge sheet against the driver of offending car bearing No.KA07M5903.
The said charge sheet admittedly remained unchallenged till date.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of offending car bearing No.KA07M5903 by its driver.

Hence, Issue No.1 is answered 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
14. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car bearing No.KA07M5903 by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: In the petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 45 years.
She has produced aadhar card at Ex.P.13 to prove her age.
As per aadhar card, her date of birth is 01.05.1974.
The accident has taken place on 04.09.2019.

Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was taken as 45 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16.
Further, the petitioner has averred that she was doing business under the name and style Lakshmi Saree House and earning a sum of Rs.70,000/p.m.
In this regard, she has not produced any documents to prove her avocation.

Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2019, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,000/ p.m.
for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
18.
The Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
As per the Wound Certificate, the Petitioner has sustained following injuries.
1.Small lacerated cut over upper right eyelid.
Incised cut wound over 1st and 2nd web.

2. Xray right humerus - fracture mid shaft of humerus.
Right hand dislocation of 1st MCP joint.
Fracture base of right 2nd metacarpal bone.
3. CT abdomen & pelvis - Blunt trauma abdomen left renal artery dissection, liver parenchymal contusion.
The doctor has opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.Nagaraj.B.N has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
19.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:

sentences.text: The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in her evidence that she was admitted as an inpatient from 0409 2019 to 13092019 and from 21.9.2019 to 28.09.2019 at Aster hospital.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 18 days.
21. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/ under this head (@
Rs.14,000/ per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
22.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
23. The Petitioner has deposed that she spent Rs.11,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
The petitioner has produced 6 medical bills at Ex.P.11 and advance receipts at Ex.P.12.
The medical bills at Ex. P.11 amounting to Rs.4,75,000/.

Since the document Ex.P.12 is advance receipts, the amounts mentioned in those documents are not accepted and the claim of sum of Rs.1,21,539/ made on the basis of said document is deducted from the claim of Rs.5,96,539/.
Moreover, the medical bills are not disputed by the respondent No.1.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.4,75,000/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

24. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent disablement and due to the injury she is completely bed ridden, getting head ache and giddiness often, cannot walk or squat on the floor, cannot use Indian toilet, cannot lift or carry weight, cannot do household work and undergoing mental shock and pain.
Even in her evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

sentences.text: Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked clinical notes and Xray at Ex.P.22 and 23.
He assessed total physical disability of right hand at 15% and whole body physical disability at 16%.
26. In the crossexamination PW.2 has stated that he has not treated the petitioner at any point of time.
He has admitted that on 24.08.2022 the petitioner approached him for the purpose of assessment of disability.
He has also admitted that petitioner got admitted on 21.09.2019 for taking treatment for jaundice and on 21.10.2019 she underwent one more surgery for removal of 'K' wiring.
He has admitted that fracture is united.
He has denied the suggestion that he has given higher rate of disability to the Petitioner.

27. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on hand and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner keeping in mind the age of the petitioner and by considering the nature of her work, upon consideration of the fact that the petitioner got examined herself before this court as PW.1 and also tendered for cross examination done at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.1 during which she could be able to give rational answers to the questions and regarding the facts of the case, I am of the opinion that disability assessed by PW.2 it would be just and proper to consider such disability at the rate of 12% and so also the physical disability assessed by the PW.2.
Considering all these aspects, this Tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable if the disability of the Petitioner is considered at 12%.
28. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the age of Petitioner is 14.

With multiplier of 14, income of Rs.14,000/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 14%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.2,82,240/ (Rs.14,000/ x 12 = 1,68,000/, Rs.1.68,000/x 14 x 12/100 = 2,82,240/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,82,240/ under this head.

FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
29.
During her evidence PW.1 deposed that she may incur future medical expenses for the removal of implants.
PW.2 deposed that approximately the petitioner might incur Rs.60,000/ to undergo surgery for removal of implants.
However, no supportive documents/estimation regarding such expenses has been produced.
PW.2 admits to have not issued any such estimation.
Considering all these factors, it appears just and proper to this court to award sum of Rs.20,000/ under head.
Accordingly same is awarded.
This amount do not carry any interest.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
30.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.4,75,000/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.2,82,240/ 7

Future medical expenses Rs. 20,000/
Total Rs.8,88,240/

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.8,88,240/ which is rounded off to Rs.8,88,250/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

31. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing No.KA07M5903.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of offending vehicle.
The Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.

Therefore,
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".

32. ISSUE No. 3 : In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.8,88,250/ along with  interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
